candidates.issues: Uses the imperative form (חממו, המיסו) which is less common than the present plural form in Israeli recipes. The verb 'מזגו' is less appropriate for batter than 'יוצקים'.
Very natural phrasing, uses the standard present-plural voice for instructions (מחממים, ממיסים, יוצקים). The translation of 'flaky sea salt' is a bit literal, but acceptable.
Translates 'chocolate chips' as 'שבבי שוקולד', which is understood but 'שוקולד צ'יפס' is the overwhelmingly standard term in Hebrew. Otherwise good phrasing.

Adds the word 'קטן' (small) to the saucepan, which isn't in the source. Uses imperative verbs instead of the standard present-plural. Translating 'flaky sea salt' to 'מלח ים אטלנטי' is very idiomatic, though.
